problem_heading: TN looks simple — until the officer says no

problem_cards.title: Your job title isn't what matters
problem_cards.body: CBP approves the duties, not the title. A "Software Engineer" offer letter with management-heavy duties, or a consultant role that reads like general business, can be refused on the spot. We match your actual duties to the USMCA occupation list before you travel.

problem_cards.title: Degree mismatches kill applications
problem_cards.body: Most TN occupations require a specific baccalaureate or credentials. A related-but-different degree, a three-year Canadian degree, or experience in place of education all need to be argued correctly — with evidence, not hope.

problem_cards.title: A refusal follows you
problem_cards.body: A border refusal goes in your record and makes every future attempt harder. The cheapest time to get legal review is before your first application — the second-cheapest is right after a refusal, before you try again.

fees_heading: What does a TN case cost?
fees_body: TN legal fees are flat and depend on whether this is a straightforward first application, a case with credential or duties complications, or a strategy reset after a refusal. Government fees are modest — the TN application fee at a port of entry is a fraction of most visa filings. We quote your exact fee during the consultation, before you commit.
who_heading: Is the TN route right for you?
who_for: You are a Canadian citizen (Mexican citizens use a different TN process we also handle)
You have — or expect — a job offer from a U.S. employer
The role fits a USMCA/NAFTA professional occupation (engineer, accountant, scientist, computer systems analyst, management consultant, and ~60 more)
You hold the required degree, license, or qualifying experience
who_not: You want to work for your own company — TN generally doesn't allow self-employment (ask us about E-2 instead)
Your role isn't on the USMCA occupation list (H-1B, O-1, or L-1 may fit)
You're seeking permanent residence as the immediate goal — TN is non-immigrant intent (we can plan the green card path separately)

faq.q: How fast can a Canadian get a TN visa?
faq.a: Canadian citizens can apply directly at a U.S. port of entry or pre-clearance airport and receive a decision the same day — no petition or consulate appointment required. The real timeline is the preparation: a well-documented application typically takes one to two weeks to assemble properly.

faq.q: What occupations qualify for TN status?
faq.a: The USMCA lists roughly 60 professions, including engineers, computer systems analysts, accountants, management consultants, scientists, teachers (college/university), and many medical roles. Each has specific degree or license requirements. If your title isn't a clean match, classification strategy decides the case — that's the core of what we do.

faq.q: Can I apply for TN with a three-year Canadian degree or without a degree?
faq.a: Sometimes. Several occupations accept alternative credentials — for example, Management Consultant allows five years of relevant experience in place of a degree, and Scientific Technician/Technologist has its own standard. These cases are more scrutinized and benefit most from legal preparation.

faq.q: What happens if I'm refused at the border?
faq.a: You're sent back the same day, the refusal is recorded, and future applications face more scrutiny. A refusal is not a ban — most refused applicants can reapply with a corrected package. If you've been refused, don't retry with the same documents; have the file reviewed first.

faq.q: How long does TN status last, and can I renew it?
faq.a: TN status is granted for up to three years at a time and can be renewed indefinitely in three-year increments, as long as the professional role and your qualifications continue. Renewals can be done at the border or by mail through USCIS.

faq.q: Can TN lead to a green card?
faq.a: TN is a non-immigrant status without dual intent, so pursuing permanent residence while on TN requires careful sequencing — commonly through employer sponsorship (PERM) or self-petitions like EB-2 NIW. If a green card is the long-term goal, we plan the transition so a pending case doesn't jeopardize your TN entries.
